note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in SD.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Badlands Loop State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SD 240 through Badlands National Park, between Cactus Flat (I-90) and Wall; Jackson and Pennington counties

facts.fact: The byway is SD Highway 240, a 39-mile loop between Cactus Flat and Wall that takes about an hour to drive without stopping.
The route has 12 designated roadside scenic overlooks and passes the Ben Reifel Visitor Center and Cedar Pass Lodge.
The gravel Sage Creek Rim Road branches off the loop.

byways.name: Native American National and State Scenic Byway
byways.designation: South Dakota State Scenic Byway and National Scenic Byway
byways.where: SD 37, 1804, 50, 1806, 34, 63, US 212, US 83 and gravel BIA 7, from Running Water (Nebraska line) to Kenel (North Dakota line); continues into North Dakota

facts.fact: The Missouri River leads the byway from the Chief Standing Bear Bridge on the Nebraska border to the North Dakota border near Kenel.
The route crosses the lands of the Yankton Sioux, Crow Creek Sioux, Lower Brule Sioux, Cheyenne River Sioux and Standing Rock Sioux tribes.

Landmarks include the 50-foot Dignity: Of Earth and Sky statue near Chamberlain, the Big Bend Dam at Fort Thompson where the byway crosses the Missouri, the Oahe Dam and the Sitting Bull Monument, a 7-ton granite bust at Mobridge.

byways.review: Travel South Dakota names it a state as well as national byway; the federal byway dataset in the catalog flags only the national designation. Shared with North Dakota.

byways.name: Peter Norbeck National Scenic Byway
byways.designation: South Dakota State Scenic Byway, National Scenic Byway and National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: SD 87 (Needles Highway), US 16A (Iron Mountain Road), SD 244 and SD 89 through Custer State Park and the Black Hills National Forest; Custer and Pennington counties

facts.fact: The byway is about 70 miles long (Forest Service) or 68 miles (Travel South Dakota) and takes in Mount Rushmore, the Needles Highway, Iron Mountain Road and Custer State Park.
The Needles Highway passes through the Needles Eye Tunnel, 8 feet wide by 9 feet 9 inches high, and the Iron Creek Tunnel.
Iron Mountain Road has three tunnels that frame Mount Rushmore in the distance and is known for its Pigtail Bridges.
Peter Norbeck, South Dakota governor and senator, laid out the Iron Mountain Road in the 1930s.

byways.review: Mileage differs between sources (68 vs 70). The Wildlife Loop Road is also listed separately as its own state byway.

byways.name: Spearfish Canyon State and National Forest Service Scenic Byway
byways.designation: South Dakota State Scenic Byway and National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 14A from Spearfish to Cheyenne Crossing (US 85); Lawrence County, Black Hills National Forest

facts.fact: The byway is 19 miles of US 14A between Spearfish and the Cheyenne Crossing junction, with Spearfish Creek on the canyon floor below limestone cliffs.
The byway follows an old railroad grade abandoned after flooding in 1933; old rail stops and mining camps include Savoy and Elmore.
Waterfalls along the canyon include Bridal Veil, Little Spearfish and Roughlock Falls; the aspens turn in September.

byways.name: Wildlife Loop State Scenic Byway
byways.where: Wildlife Loop Road in Custer State Park, between US 16A near the east entrance and SD 87 near the Blue Bell entrance; Custer County

facts.fact: Wildlife Loop Road is 18 miles long and twists through prairie and ponderosa pine hills in Custer State Park.
The park holds about 1,350 free-roaming bison, plus prairie dogs and a band of feral burros.
The burros are often near the road's southeastern tip and beg for snacks; a state park entrance license is required.

byways.review: Travel South Dakota's page is also a good link: https://www.travelsouthdakota.com/trip-ideas/story/wildlife-loop-state-scenic-byway

issues: SDDOT's page says South Dakota has six State Scenic Byways but names none; only five could be identified (the five catalog roads). SDDOT's 2002 page said five and its 2006 page six, so a sixth was designated between 2002 and 2006. Candidates not confirmed on any official page: a separately designated piece of the Native American Scenic Byway, or a road such as Skyline Drive (Hot Springs) mentioned by secondary sources. Ask the SDDOT Scenic Byways Coordinator or check Transportation Commission minutes from 2002-2006.
byways.org (archived 2012) listed the same five roads; Travel South Dakota pages cross-link the same five and no more.
The federal catalog data flags the Native American Scenic Byway as national only; Travel South Dakota titles it a National and State Scenic Byway, which is how it is listed here.
Peter Norbeck mileage differs: 68 miles (Travel South Dakota) vs 70 miles (USFS); catalog maps 69.
Spearfish Canyon is 19 miles per Travel South Dakota; catalog maps 21.5. Badlands Loop is 39 miles per Travel South Dakota; catalog maps 38.
Wildlife Loop Road catalog line maps 15.6 miles vs 18 miles stated by SD Game, Fish and Parks; may be missing a short piece at one end.
